title: A secret, shouted across a room
hook: How do two strangers agree on a secret when a spy hears every word they say?
claim: Diffie-Hellman lets two people build the same secret from public mixtures, because mixing is easy and un-mixing is hard.

worked_example.setup: public p=23, g=5; Alice secret 6, Bob secret 15
worked_example.result: both get 2; the spy's combination gives 14

key_moment: Alice's and Bob's final pots glow the same amber; the spy's pot is mud (14 != 2)
naive_first: the spy just mixes the two public pots
twist: un-mixing is the hard part: a counter tries x = 1, 2, 3... toy finds 6; at 617 digits it never ends
scale: smallest RFC 7919 group: 2048-bit prime, 617 digits; TLS 1.3 uses (EC)DHE
misconception: the secret key is sent across the network, encrypted
recurring_object: three glowing paint pots on a dark reflective floor (Alice, spy, Bob)
plants: the padlock: next episode, how do you know you're talking to the real Bob?
